newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline ends firmer, higher NYMEX draws buyer.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline ends firmer, higher NYMEX draws buyer.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices ended firmer in line with crude and NYMEX unleaded futures and with some good buying interest for barges beginning to emerge, traders said.
They said the market carried a more bullish tone with firmer U.S. markets drawing fresh buying interest for barges from key inland markets and supporting a fairly well supplied cargo market.

"Some people are expecting gasoline to make a move higher and this has created some pockets of buying interest," one trader said. "There hasn't been much buying from Germany recently so they may come in again soon but there's plenty of oil around," he added.

Traders said the trans-Atlantic arbitrage window appeared nearly ready to reopen. Some saw a gap of $3 a tonne but others said an increase in New York gasoline prices of about 0.50 cent a gallon or decrease in prices in Europe of the same level would reopen trans-Atlantic trading opportunities and take some pressure of the lengthy NWE market.
Eurograde barges put on around $1 in early business with trade at $182.50 and $183 a tonne fob ARA.
Cargo prices were steady with Eurograde cargoes valued around $188 a tonne cif NWE.
